description: Office security policies. Detects policy violations even when traffic is technically non-malicious. Edit to match your organization's security stance.

anonymizer_detection.description: Detect use of anonymization networks on corporate devices

tor.notes: Tor usage on corporate network = potential data exfiltration or C2 hiding

i2p.notes: I2P is rarely legitimate on corporate networks

vpn_unauthorized.notes: Unauthorized VPN bypasses corporate security controls

proxy.notes: SOCKS (1080) / Squid (3128) / Privoxy (8118). Port 8080 (http-alt) intentionally excluded — it is used by countless legitimate internal web services (Jenkins, GitLab, Tomcat, custom apps). Flagging it as an anonymizer was the pre-0.1 default and produced ~660/min alerts on any office LAN running an internal web app.

zeronet.notes: ZeroNet decentralized network — no legitimate corporate use

device_restrictions.description: Certain device types should NEVER use certain protocols

rules.reason: IoT/OT device using anonymizer/VPN = compromised device
IoT device connecting to management/C2 ports = compromised
Workstation using dark web network = policy violation

time_based_policies.description: Activity outside business hours gets elevated severity
time_based_policies.notes: Tor at 3am is more suspicious than Tor at 2pm

Finance.reason: Finance handles confidential data — anonymizer = exfiltration risk

IoT.reason: IoT devices should have minimal network footprint

Guest.reason: Guests may use VPN but not dark web networks

IT.notes: IT staff may legitimately test anonymizers — lower severity

authorized_vpn.description: IPs/users authorized to use VPN. Everyone else flagged.
authorized_vpn.notes: Corporate VPN servers — connections TO these are legitimate

data_exfiltration_indicators.description: Patterns that suggest data leaving the organization

rules.name: large_upload_to_anonymizer
rules.reason: Large data upload through anonymizer = exfiltration

rules.name: dns_tunneling_indicators
rules.reason: Oversized DNS with long query names = possible DNS tunneling

rules.name: encrypted_to_rare_country
rules.condition: dst_port == 443 AND dst_ip NOT in known_services AND duration > 3600
rules.reason: Long-lived encrypted connection to unknown server
